techniques.name: Classic Boogie Shuffle & Pinky Stretch (A5 - A6 - A7)
techniques.description: Steady swinging shuffle pattern fretting the root note while alternating the 5th, 6th, and minor 7th with the pinky finger

notes: A5 / A6: Open A string + 2nd fret D string (A5), reaching to 4th fret D string with ring/pinky (A6), and 5th fret (A7)
D5 / D6: Open D string + 2nd fret G string (D5), reaching to 4th fret G string (D6), and 5th fret (D7)
E5 / E6: Open E string + 2nd fret A string (E5), reaching to 4th fret A string (E6), and 5th fret (E7)
sequence: Establish the swung eighth-note pulse ('DAH-dum, DAH-dum') at 136 BPM
Keep the index finger barred across fret 2 while bouncing the pinky on fret 4 and 5
Apply light right-hand palm muting near the bridge saddles for percussive chug
tips: Keep your thumb positioned behind the neck centerline to facilitate the pinky fret-4 reach
If the pinky stretch cramps your hand, rotate your fretting wrist slightly forward
Dial in a touch of slapback delay (120ms) for that vintage 1971 Sun Records bounce
details.progression: A - D - A - E - D - A

techniques.name: Ross Hannaford's Chuck Berry Double-Stops
techniques.description: Holding 5th fret on strings 1 and 2 while bending the 7th fret G string, creating authentic rockabilly bite

notes: Double stop at 5th fret: strings 1 (E) and 2 (E) barred with index finger pad
Bend at 7th fret string 3 (D to E full step)
Sliding 6th intervals: 4th fret G + 5th fret high E sliding to 6th fret G + 7th fret high E
sequence: Bend string 3 at fret 7 with ring and middle fingers
Strike strings 2 and 1 at fret 5 together with a downstroke
Add quarter-tone blues micro-bends on the minor 3rd (string 3, fret 5)
tips: Keep your index finger flat across both strings 1 and 2
Use hybrid picking (pick on string 3, middle finger plucking string 1) for sharper transient attack
Let the slapback echo create an artificial doubling effect on every pluck

sections.name: Intro Boogie Shuffle Riff
sections.description: Ross Wilson's irresistible opening boogie groove that kicked off the 1970s Australian pub rock revolution.
notes: Swing the eighth notes heavily with a triplet bounce feel
Light palm muting on the low strings
Keep the index finger firmly anchored on fret 2 of the D string

sections.name: Verse 1 Shuffle & Vocal Call
sections.description: Opening verse ('Now listen everybody got to tell you 'bout a dance') featuring boogie shuffle and syncopated double-stop stabs.
sections.progression: A - D - A - E - D - A
notes: Lock into the rhythm section's steady walking swing
Ross Hannaford answers Ross Wilson's vocal phrases with sharp 5th-fret double stops
Keep the volume controlled to leave room for the lead vocal

sections.name: Chorus Singalong
sections.description: The immortal 'Doing the Eagle Rock' chorus with full open chord strums and party vocal energy.
sections.progression: A - D - A - E - D - A
notes: Open up into ringing open chords
Accent beats 2 and 4 with sharp snap
Finish with the quick chromatic walkdown turnaround

sections.name: Verse 2 Lead Fills & 6th Intervals
sections.description: Hannaford expands the verse arrangement with sweet sliding 6th intervals across strings 1 and 3.
sections.progression: A - D - A - E - D - A
notes: Slide up into the 6th interval at fret 6 and 7 smoothly
Dampen strings with fretting fingers immediately after striking for crisp punch
Listen to the dialogue between the vocal melody and guitar fills

sections.name: Ross Hannaford's Main Guitar Solo
sections.description: One of the most celebrated guitar solos in Australian rock history: pure Chuck Berry rock-and-roll joy bursting with double stops, micro-tonal blues curls, and chromatic transitions across the 12-bar form.
sections.progression: A - D - A - E - D - A
notes: Bars 1-4: Bend the 7th fret G string while holding the 5th fret on strings 1 and 2
Bars 5-6 (over D): Shift up to the 10th fret double-stop position on strings 1 and 2
Bars 9-10 (over E): Hit the 12th fret double-stop and walk down chromatically (12 -> 11 -> 10) into the resolution
Slapback delay (110ms) creates the signature vintage bouncy slap

sections.name: Chromatic Turnaround Lick
sections.description: The classic 1950s rockabilly chromatic turnaround resolving from E to D to A.
notes: Walk down chromatically on the A string: 7 -> 6 -> 5 -> 4 into open A
Hit the sharp E7#9 or open E7 dominant turnaround on beat 4
Sets up the explosive return of the final chorus

sections.name: Outro Solo & Boogie Jam Fade
sections.technique: High Register Blues Bends & Vocal Trading
sections.description: Ross Hannaford takes a fiery second solo climbing into the upper register as the party energy reaches fever pitch.
sections.progression: A - D - A - E - D - A (repeating to fade)
notes: Climb up into 14th and 15th fret bends on strings 1 and 2
Trade licks rhythmically with Ross Wilson's scat vocal calls
Maintain relaxed wrist motion through the extended four-minute jam

beginner.title: Open Chords & Strumming the Progression
steps: Learn open A, D, and E chords cleanly
Practice the 12-bar blues progression in A at 100 BPM
Count the swung eighth notes out loud ('1-and-2-and-3-and-4-and')
beginner.goals: Solid timekeeping through the entire 12-bar form

intermediate.title: The Boogie-Woogie Pinky Stretch
steps: Master the A5 to A6 to A7 pinky stretch on strings 5 and 4
Move the exact same grip to D5/D6 and E5/E6
Build stamina at 136 BPM using our Metronome Speed Trainer
intermediate.goals: Fluid boogie shuffle without hand fatigue or dropped beats

advanced.title: Ross Hannaford's Solo & Double-Stops
steps: Learn Ross Hannaford's sliding double-stops at fret 5 across strings 1 and 2
Master the full-step 7th-fret G string bend held behind the 5th-fret double stop
Nail the chromatic turnaround walkdown at 2:15 and high-register outro solo
advanced.goals: Complete stage-ready transcription of one of Australia's greatest guitar solos

commonMistakes: Playing straight eighth notes instead of the essential swung shuffle groove
Letting the unused open strings ring out and muddy the boogie riff
Collapsing the left-hand wrist against the neck, making the fret 4 stretch difficult
Rushing through the double-stop bends in the solo without letting the slapback echo breathe
practiceRoutine: Warm up with 5 minutes of pinky independence exercises on frets 2, 4, and 5
Run the boogie shuffle in A with our Metronome set to 'Shuffle' groove preset
Isolate the main guitar solo (bars 1-12) at 100 BPM before ramping to 136 BPM
Practice sliding 6th intervals across strings 1 and 3
focusAreas: Fretting-hand wrist relaxation during pinky stretches
Accurate pitch on the 7th-fret G string bend in the solo
metronomeWork: Select the 'Blues Shuffle' sound preset on our Metronome tool
Start at 105 BPM and practice clean shuffle accents
Work up to the studio tempo of 136 BPM in 5 BPM increments
Practice solo double-stops at half tempo to guarantee crisp articulation
